investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 eligible nodes, and the 4 remaining nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or node selector requirements. With 0/6 nodes schedulable and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote agent pod is stuck unscheduled, preventing VM provisioning from starting and causing all downstream evidence (vmIdPresent, remoteState) to go uncollected. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
proof: failed-check.message: '0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.'
failed-check.timing: status=fail latencyMs=152767, pod stuck unscheduled for 146s before the check timed out.
failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty — no orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState was written, consistent with the pod never reaching a running state.
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all 4 required evidence keys (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent.

sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical Unschedulable message, pod stuck for 147s, no evidence collected.
source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1877-1885: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) — the agent pod must be scheduled before any evidence can be written.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState in [running, idle, ready], neither of which can be satisfied without a scheduled pod.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new remote agent pods. Supported directly by failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, and sibling.remote-agent-runtime.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 non-kata nodes do not match the pod's required affinity, meaning the schedulable pool is permanently limited to 2 nodes. If those 2 nodes are at capacity, any new pod is immediately unschedulable.

Tertiary — cluster under-provisioning: the total number of kata.peerpods.io/vm slots across the 2 eligible nodes may be too small for concurrent eval runs plus live workloads, causing transient or sustained exhaustion.

Lower confidence — a recent infrastructure change reduced the number of kata-capable nodes from a previously larger pool, shrinking available capacity. No infrastructure change evidence is present in the supplied packet; this remains speculative.

Consider a dedicated eval for the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource health that runs independently of agent creation, so infrastructure capacity issues are reported separately from agent lifecycle correctness.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing — Kubernetes Cluster Exhausted of kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-04T15:42–15:47Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the eval's remote agent pod because only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both are fully exhausted, while the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs:1905) never returned an agent, and no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was ever written, causing the contract validation to fail completely.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent provisioning path has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource across all eligible nodes. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that no VM slot was available on either of the two kata-peerpods-capable nodes, and preemption was not possible. The pod remained Unschedulable for ~144–147 seconds across all three checks before the eval timed out. This is an infrastructure-layer capacity constraint, not a code defect in the eval runner or contract definitions. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the packet; this is an eval-layer failure indicating the remote-agents feature is currently unable to provision new VMs in the production-api environment.

possibleCauses: kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the two eligible nodes: both kata-peerpods-capable nodes in the 6-node cluster are fully allocated, leaving no VM slots for new eval pods. This is the primary cause directly stated in the scheduler message (failed-check.message).

Node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote agent pod requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, reducing the schedulable pool to those 2 nodes. If those 2 nodes are saturated, no fallback exists.

Concurrent remote agent workloads consuming all available kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: other production workloads or concurrent eval runs may have claimed all VM slots on the two eligible nodes before this eval's pod was submitted.
Insufficient node pool scaling: the cluster may lack autoscaling for kata-peerpods-capable nodes, or autoscaling was not triggered in time to satisfy the pod before the eval timeout.

Eval concurrency: all three sibling checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) ran within a ~5-minute window and each attempted to provision a separate remote agent pod, potentially competing for the same exhausted resource pool.

Because the agent pod could never be scheduled, the eval runner never reached the point of collecting any evidence, leaving all 5 required contract fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) absent.

Preemption was also unavailable on both eligible nodes. As a direct consequence, the createAgent call in the eval runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 1918) never completed, no agent was provisioned, and the check timed out after ~147 seconds with an empty evidence payload — violating the remote-agent-runtime expected-output contract which requires orgId, agentId, model, provider, and message.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 eligible nodes, and the 4 remaining nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or node selector requirements. With 0/6 nodes schedulable and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote agent pod is stuck unscheduled, preventing VM provisioning from starting and causing all downstream evidence (vmIdPresent, remoteState) to go uncollected. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
proof: failed-check.message: '0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.'
failed-check.timing: status=fail latencyMs=152767, pod stuck unscheduled for 146s before the check timed out.
failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty — no orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState was written, consistent with the pod never reaching a running state.
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all 4 required evidence keys (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent.
sibling.remote-agent-state: identical Unschedulable message, pod stuck for 144s, no evidence collected.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical Unschedulable message, pod stuck for 147s, no evidence collected.
source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1877-1885: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) — the agent pod must be scheduled before any evidence can be written.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState in [running, idle, ready], neither of which can be satisfied without a scheduled pod.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new remote agent pods. Supported directly by failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, and sibling.remote-agent-runtime.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 non-kata nodes do not match the pod's required affinity, meaning the schedulable pool is permanently limited to 2 nodes. If those 2 nodes are at capacity, any new pod is immediately unschedulable.

Tertiary — cluster under-provisioning: the total number of kata.peerpods.io/vm slots across the 2 eligible nodes may be too small for concurrent eval runs plus live workloads, causing transient or sustained exhaustion.

Lower confidence — a recent infrastructure change reduced the number of kata-capable nodes from a previously larger pool, shrinking available capacity. No infrastructure change evidence is present in the supplied packet; this remains speculative.

investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent pod on any of the 6 available cluster nodes: the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not satisfy the pod's node affinity or node selector constraints. Preemption was also unavailable on both eligible nodes. As a direct consequence, the createAgent call in the eval runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 1918) never completed, no agent was provisioned, and the check timed out after ~147 seconds with an empty evidence payload — violating the remote-agent-runtime expected-output contract which requires orgId, agentId, model, provider, and message.
proof: failed-check.message: 'pod stuck unscheduled for 147s (Unschedulable): 0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.'
failed-check.timing: status=fail latencyMs=151585 endedAt=2026-07-04T15:47:35.190Z — eval ran for ~151 seconds before failing, consistent with a scheduling timeout rather than an API error.
failed-check.evidence: empty object {} — no evidence was collected at all, confirming the agent pod never started.
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all 5 required fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are absent, consistent with the runner never reaching the createAgent call result.
sibling.remote-agent-create: same Unschedulable message, latencyMs=152767, endedAt=2026-07-04T15:42:36.989Z — the create check failed first with the identical scheduler error.
sibling.remote-agent-state: same Unschedulable message, latencyMs=146616, endedAt=2026-07-04T15:45:03.605Z — the state check failed next with the identical scheduler error.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1910-1918: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1918; a scheduling failure here would prevent any evidence from being returned.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:262-270: remote-agent-runtime contract requires orgId, agentId, model, provider, message and asserts message containsIgnoreCase 'hello from aura' — none of these could be satisfied without a running pod.
possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: all available VM slots are consumed by existing pods, leaving no capacity for new remote agent pods. No preemption victims were found, meaning no lower-priority pods could be evicted to free capacity.

[Likely contributing] Node affinity or node selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote agent pod spec requires a label or taint that only the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm nodes carry, so the effective scheduling pool is already limited to those 2 nodes before capacity is even checked.

[Possible] Cluster under-provisioning: the total kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity across the 2 eligible nodes may be too small for the concurrent load of eval probes plus production workloads, causing contention during the eval run window.
[Possible] A resource quota or limit range at the namespace level may be restricting additional VM-backed pod creation beyond what the node-level resource already shows.

[Low likelihood] A node or node-pool that previously provided kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity may have been cordoned, drained, or removed, reducing the eligible node count from a previously larger pool to the current 2.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If the kata.peerpods.io/vm nodes show available (unallocated) VM capacity at the time of the failure, the exhaustion hypothesis would be weakened and a different scheduling constraint (e.g., a quota, a taint, or a broken node) would need to be investigated.
If a re-run of the eval immediately after the failure succeeds and collects all 5 required evidence fields, the issue was transient capacity contention rather than a sustained resource exhaustion.

If only remote-agent-runtime failed while remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state passed in the same run window, the root cause would be localized to the runtime check's pod spec rather than a shared cluster-level capacity problem.

If the 4 non-kata nodes also carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and the node affinity mismatch is the sole blocker, fixing the affinity/selector would resolve the issue without requiring additional VM capacity.

If cluster event logs show a node eviction, scale-down, or cordon event immediately before 2026-07-04T15:42Z (the time of the first sibling failure), the cause would be a node removal rather than gradual capacity exhaustion.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval that checks kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity on eligible nodes before attempting remote agent creation, surfacing resource exhaustion as a distinct check status rather than a scheduling timeout.
Add a cluster node-pool health check eval that verifies the expected number of kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes are Ready and have non-zero allocatable VM capacity.

Add a scheduling latency eval that measures pod-to-running time for remote agent pods and warns when it exceeds a threshold (e.g., 30s), catching capacity pressure before it causes full scheduling failures.

Consider adding a remote-agent-create retry eval that distinguishes between a transient scheduling delay and a sustained Unschedulable condition, to differentiate capacity spikes from structural exhaustion.
